system_prompt:
You are a twelfth-grade student in the final year of secondary school who has taken advanced mathematics courses, taking the TIMSS Advanced mathematics test for students like you. Do your best on each question, as you would on a real test, using the mathematics you have learned in school so far.

The pictures, figures, and graphs of the test booklet are described in words, and its tables are written out. When a question asks you to draw, mark, shade, label, or fill in something on a figure, graph, or table, describe exactly what you would draw or write, and where. When a question asks you to show your work or explain your answer, include the work or explanation in your answer. For a multiple-choice question, choose one option.
user_prompt:
In the ΔABC the altitudes BN and CM intersect at point S. The measure of ∠MSB is 40° and the measure of ∠SBC is 20°. Write a PROOF of the following statement:

“ΔABC is isosceles.”

Give geometric reasons for statements in your proof.

[Image: Triangle ABC with altitudes BN and CM intersecting at S]

Figure, described in words:
A triangle ABC with vertex A at the top, vertex B at the bottom left, and vertex C at the bottom right. Segment BN is an altitude drawn from B to AC, with a right-angle symbol at N. Segment CM is an altitude drawn from C to AB, with a right-angle symbol at M. BN and CM intersect at interior point S. The angle MSB is marked with an arc and labeled 40°. The angle SBC is marked with an arc and labeled 20°.

answer.description: Your answer to the question, as you would write it in the test booklet, with any work, explanation, or description of a drawing that the question asks for.
answer.title: Answer

output.answer:
Since CM is an altitude to AB, CM ⟂ AB. As S lies on CM and M lies on AB, ∠SMB = 90°. In ΔMSB, ∠MSB = 40°, so ∠SBM = 180° − 90° − 40° = 50°. Because B, M, A are collinear, ∠ABC = ∠SBM + ∠SBC = 50° + 20° = 70°.

Since BN is an altitude to AC, BN ⟂ AC. As S lies on BN and N lies on AC, ∠BNC = 90°. Also, ∠BSC and ∠MSB are vertically opposite angles, so ∠BSC = 40°. In ΔBSC, ∠BCS = 180° − 90° − 40° = 50°. Since C, S, M are collinear, ∠BCA = ∠BCS = 50°.

Therefore ∠BAC = 180° − 70° − 50° = 60°. This does not give equal angles in ΔABC, so the stated conclusion cannot be proved from the given information: the angles are 70°, 50°, and 60°, and thus ΔABC is not isosceles.
